picks.excerpt: KOMCA's amended rules took effect August 3, ending South Korea's blanket ban on registering AI-assisted songs — but writers must now declare AI use, with false filings risking royalty holds and contract termination. Changes how Korean songwriters document an AI-touched session.
picks.rationale: Korean songwriters can finally register AI-assisted works — with a mandatory disclosure that changes session documentation from August 3.

picks.excerpt: Majors and indies jointly proposed chart-eligibility rules for AI: only AI-assisted tracks may chart, only legitimate AI tools may be used, and AI use must be labelled. A labelling standard that will land directly in artists' release workflow.
picks.rationale: Majors and indies agree on the first chart-eligibility standard for AI tracks — labelling becomes part of the release checklist.

picks.excerpt: CDM spots an emerging scene of producers deliberately recording strange or 'bad' music in the hope AI scrapers will train on it — data poisoning as a creative genre. A craft-level response to generative models that turns the training pipeline itself into material.
picks.rationale: Producers are turning scraper data-poisoning into an actual genre — the training pipeline itself becomes creative material.

picks.excerpt: A London 'sound-free concert' used generative AI music platforms plus Bluetooth-connected cochlear implants to stream audio directly to d/Deaf attendees. Generative music as an accessibility design surface rather than a content firehose.
picks.rationale: Generative music paired with cochlear implants turns a concert into an accessibility design problem, not a content-volume one.

picks.excerpt: Music Ally revisits Fenix Flexin's viral 'Rubberz' and the accusations that it is AI-generated, pulling apart why the question is now almost unanswerable when most DAW tools already embed AI. A useful test case for where 'AI-assisted' ends and 'AI-generated' begins.
picks.rationale: A charting viral hit shows the 'AI-assisted vs AI-generated' line is now nearly undecidable — the exact line the new chart rules depend on.
